units.zh: 田叔者，趙陘城人也。
units.en: Tian Shu was a native of Xingcheng in the state of Zhao.
units.literal: Tian Shu was a person from Xingcheng in Zhao.

units.zh: 其先，齊田氏苗裔也。
units.en: His forebears were descendants of the Tian clan of the state of Qi.
units.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Tian clan of Qi.

units.zh: 叔喜劍，學黃老術於樂巨公所。
units.en: Tian Shu delighted in swordsmanship and studied the teachings of Huang-Lao philosophy under the master Yue Jugong.
units.literal: Shu enjoyed swordsmanship, and studied the arts of Huang-Lao at the place of Yue Jugong.

units.zh: 叔為人刻廉自喜，喜游諸公。
units.en: By nature, Tian Shu was rigorously principled and incorruptible, taking pride in these qualities, and he enjoyed keeping company with distinguished men.
units.literal: Shu as a person was strict, incorruptible, and self-possessed, and enjoyed associating with various notables.

units.zh: 趙人舉之趙相趙午，午言之趙王張敖所，趙王以為郎中。
units.en: The people of Zhao recommended him to the state chancellor Zhao Wu, who in turn spoke of him to King Zhang Ao of Zhao. The king appointed him as a Gentleman of the Palace.
units.literal: People of Zhao recommended him to Zhao's chancellor Zhao Wu, and Wu spoke of him to the King of Zhao, Zhang Ao, and the King of Zhao appointed him as a court gentleman.

units.zh: 數歲，切直廉平，趙王賢之，未及遷。
units.en: Over the course of several years, Tian Shu proved himself forthright, incorruptible, and even-handed. The King of Zhao esteemed him as a man of worth, though he had not yet found occasion to promote him.
units.literal: After several years, being earnest, upright, incorruptible, and fair, the King of Zhao regarded him as worthy, but had not yet promoted him.

units.zh: 會陳豨反代，漢七年，高祖往誅之，過趙，趙王張敖自持案進食，禮恭甚，高祖箕踞罵之。
units.en: It happened that Chen Xi raised a rebellion in the territory of Dai. In the seventh year of the Han dynasty, Emperor Gaozu set out to suppress him and passed through Zhao along the way. King Zhang Ao personally held the serving tray to present food to the emperor, his courtesy exceedingly respectful. But the emperor sat sprawled with his legs apart and berated the king.
units.literal: It happened that Chen Xi rebelled in Dai; in the seventh year of Han, the High Ancestor went to punish him and passed through Zhao, where the King of Zhao, Zhang Ao, personally held the serving tray to present food, his ritual courtesy being extremely respectful, but the High Ancestor sat with legs spread and berated him.

units.zh: 是時趙相趙午等數十人皆怒，謂張王曰：「王事上禮備矣，今遇王如是，臣等請為亂。」
units.en: At this, the state chancellor Zhao Wu and some dozens of other officials were all outraged. They addressed King Zhang Ao: "Your Majesty has served the emperor with every proper courtesy, yet he treats you in this manner. We, your servants, beg leave to rise in revolt."
units.literal: At that time, Zhao's chancellor Zhao Wu and dozens of others were all furious and said to King Zhang: "Your Majesty has served His Majesty with complete ritual courtesy, yet now he treats you like this; we your servants request permission to cause a disturbance."

units.zh: 趙王齧指出血，曰：「先人失國，微陛下，臣等當蟲出。
units.en: The King of Zhao bit his own finger until it bled and said: "Our forefathers lost the kingdom. Were it not for His Majesty, we would be no better than worms crawling from the earth.
units.literal: The King of Zhao bit his finger until it bled and said: "Our ancestors lost the state; without His Majesty, we your servants would be like worms crawling forth.

units.zh: 公等柰何言若是！
units.en: How dare you speak in such a way!
units.literal: How can you gentlemen speak like this!

units.zh: 毋復出口矣！」
units.en: Never let such words leave your lips again!"
units.literal: Do not let this come from your mouths again!"

units.zh: 於是貫高等曰：「王長者，不倍德。」
units.en: At this, Guan Gao and the others said among themselves: "The king is a man of honor who would never repay kindness with treachery."
units.literal: Thereupon Guan Gao and others said: "The king is a man of virtue and will not betray kindness."

units.zh: 卒私相與謀弒上。
units.en: In the end, they secretly plotted among themselves to assassinate the emperor.
units.literal: In the end they privately conspired together to assassinate the sovereign.

units.zh: 會事發覺，漢下詔捕趙王及群臣反者。
units.en: The conspiracy was eventually exposed, and the Han court issued an edict ordering the arrest of the King of Zhao along with all the ministers involved in the plot.
units.literal: It happened that the affair was discovered, and the Han court issued an edict to arrest the King of Zhao and the rebellious ministers.

units.zh: 於是趙午等皆自殺，唯貫高就系。
units.en: Zhao Wu and the other conspirators all took their own lives. Only Guan Gao submitted himself to arrest.
units.literal: Thereupon Zhao Wu and the others all killed themselves; only Guan Gao submitted to arrest.

units.zh: 是時漢下詔書：「趙有敢隨王者罪三族。」
units.en: At that time, the Han court issued a decree: "Any person of Zhao who dares follow the king shall be punished together with all three branches of their clan."
units.literal: At that time the Han court issued an edict: "Anyone in Zhao who dares follow the king shall have their three clans punished."

units.zh: 唯孟舒、田叔等十餘人赭衣自髡鉗，稱王家奴，隨趙王敖至長安。
units.en: Only Meng Shu, Tian Shu, and some ten others donned the red garments of convicts, shaved their heads and clamped iron collars around their own necks. Calling themselves slaves of the royal household, they followed King Ao of Zhao all the way to Chang'an.
units.literal: Only Meng Shu, Tian Shu, and more than ten others wore prisoner's red garments, shaved their own heads and placed iron collars on themselves, calling themselves slaves of the king's household, and followed King Ao of Zhao to Chang'an.

units.zh: 貫高事明白，趙王敖得出，廢為宣平侯，乃進言田叔等十餘人。
units.en: When Guan Gao's testimony cleared the king's name, King Ao of Zhao was released but demoted to the rank of Marquis of Xuanping. He then put forward the names of Tian Shu and more than ten others.
units.literal: When Guan Gao's affair was made clear, King Ao of Zhao was allowed to go free and was demoted to the Marquis of Xuanping; he then recommended Tian Shu and more than ten others.

units.zh: 上盡召見，與語，漢廷臣毋能出其右者，上說，盡拜為郡守、諸侯相。
units.en: The emperor summoned them all for an audience and conversed with each in turn. He found that none of the ministers at the Han court could surpass them in ability. Delighted, the emperor appointed every one of them as either a commandery governor or a chancellor to one of the feudal kings.
units.literal: The emperor summoned and received them all, and conversed with them; none among the Han court ministers could surpass them. The emperor was pleased and appointed them all as commandery governors or chancellors of feudal kingdoms.

units.zh: 叔為漢中守十餘年，會高后崩，諸呂作亂，大臣誅之，立孝文帝。
units.en: Tian Shu served as Governor of Hanzhong for more than ten years. Then Empress Dowager Gao died, and the Lü clan attempted to seize power. The senior ministers suppressed the Lü faction and placed Emperor Wen on the throne.
units.literal: Shu served as governor of Hanzhong for more than ten years. It happened that Empress Dowager Gao died, the various Lü clan members caused a rebellion, the great ministers executed them, and established Emperor Xiaowen.

units.zh: 孝文帝既立，召田叔問之曰：「公知天下長者乎？」
units.en: After Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he summoned Tian Shu and asked: "Do you know who the truly worthy men of the realm are?"
units.literal: After Emperor Xiaowen was established, he summoned Tian Shu and asked him: "Do you know who the men of virtue in the empire are?"

units.zh: 對曰：「臣何足以知之！」
units.en: Tian Shu replied: "How could your humble servant presume to know such a thing!"
units.literal: He replied: "How could your servant be sufficient to know this!"

units.zh: 上曰：「公，長者也，宜知之。」
units.en: The emperor said: "You yourself are a man of worth. Surely you would know."
units.literal: The emperor said: "You, sir, are a man of virtue yourself, and should know them."

units.zh: 叔頓首曰：「故雲中守孟舒，長者也。」
units.en: Tian Shu pressed his forehead to the ground and said: "The former Governor of Yunzhong, Meng Shu—he is truly a man of worth."
units.literal: Shu bowed his head to the ground and said: "The former governor of Yunzhong, Meng Shu, is a man of virtue."

units.zh: 是時孟舒坐虜大入塞盜劫，雲中尤甚，免。
units.en: At that time, Meng Shu had been dismissed from office because barbarian raiders had broken through the frontier defenses on a massive scale, with the Yunzhong commandery suffering the worst of it.
units.literal: At that time Meng Shu had been dismissed for the crime of barbarians making a great incursion past the frontier to raid and plunder, with Yunzhong being hit especially hard.

units.zh: 上曰：「先帝置孟舒雲中十餘年矣，虜曾一人，孟舒不能堅守，毋故士卒戰死者數百人。
units.en: The emperor said: "The late emperor posted Meng Shu at Yunzhong for more than ten years. When the barbarians once raided in force, Meng Shu failed to hold his ground, and several hundred soldiers died in battle without cause.
units.literal: The emperor said: "The former emperor placed Meng Shu in Yunzhong for more than ten years; when the barbarians once invaded, Meng Shu could not hold the defense, and for no good reason several hundred soldiers died in battle.

units.zh: 長者固殺人乎？
units.en: Does a worthy man send people to their deaths like this?
units.literal: Does a man of virtue truly cause people to be killed?

units.zh: 公何以言孟舒為長者也？」
units.en: On what basis do you call Meng Shu a man of worth?"
units.literal: On what grounds do you say that Meng Shu is a man of virtue?"

units.zh: 叔叩頭對曰：「是乃孟舒所以為長者也。
units.en: Tian Shu kowtowed and replied: "This is precisely the reason Meng Shu is a man of worth.
units.literal: Shu knocked his head on the ground and replied: "This is precisely why Meng Shu is a man of virtue.

units.zh: 夫貫高等謀反，上下明詔，趙有敢隨張王，罪三族。
units.en: When Guan Gao and the others plotted their rebellion, the throne issued a clear decree that anyone in Zhao who dared follow King Zhang Ao would be punished along with all three branches of their clan.
units.literal: When Guan Gao and the others plotted rebellion, a clear edict was issued from above: anyone in Zhao who dared follow King Zhang would have the three clans punished.

units.zh: 然孟舒自髡鉗，隨張王敖之所在，欲以身死之，豈自知為雲中守哉！
units.en: Yet Meng Shu shaved his head and clamped an iron collar around his own neck, following King Zhang Ao wherever he went, willing to lay down his life for his lord—how could he have foreseen that he would one day become Governor of Yunzhong!
units.literal: Yet Meng Shu shaved his own head and put on an iron collar, followed King Zhang Ao wherever he was, willing to die for him with his own body—how could he have known he would become governor of Yunzhong!

units.zh: 漢與楚相距，士卒罷敝。
units.en: While Han and Chu were locked in their great struggle, the soldiers had been worn down to exhaustion.
units.literal: Han and Chu confronted each other, and the soldiers were exhausted and worn out.

units.zh: 匈奴冒頓新服北夷，來為邊害，孟舒知士卒罷敝，不忍出言，士爭臨城死敵，如子為父，弟為兄，以故死者數百人。
units.en: The Xiongnu under Modu Chanyu, having recently subjugated the northern tribes, came to raid the frontier. Meng Shu knew his soldiers were utterly spent and could not bring himself to order them out to battle. Yet the men fought of their own accord, mounting the walls and throwing themselves at the enemy as sons would for their fathers and younger brothers for their elders. For this reason several hundred perished.
units.literal: The Xiongnu under Modu had newly subjugated the northern barbarians and came to harry the borders. Meng Shu knew the soldiers were exhausted and could not bear to drive them out to fight, yet the soldiers vied with one another to mount the walls and fight the enemy to the death, as sons would for fathers and younger brothers for elder brothers, and for this reason several hundred died.

units.zh: 孟舒豈故驅戰之哉！
units.en: How could Meng Shu have willfully driven them to fight!
units.literal: How could Meng Shu have deliberately driven them into battle!

units.zh: 是乃孟舒所以為長者也。」
units.en: This is precisely what makes Meng Shu a man of worth."
units.literal: This is why Meng Shu is a man of virtue."

units.zh: 於是上曰：「賢哉孟舒！」
units.en: At this, the emperor exclaimed: "What a worthy man Meng Shu is!"
units.literal: Thereupon the emperor said: "How worthy is Meng Shu!"

units.zh: 復召孟舒以為雲中守。
units.en: He summoned Meng Shu back and reappointed him as Governor of Yunzhong.
units.literal: He recalled Meng Shu and again appointed him as governor of Yunzhong.

units.zh: 後數歲，叔坐法失官。
units.en: Several years later, Tian Shu was convicted of a legal offense and stripped of his post.
units.literal: Several years later, Shu was found guilty of a legal offense and lost his position.

units.zh: 梁孝王使人殺故吳相袁盎，景帝召田叔案梁，具得其事，還報。
units.en: King Xiao of Liang sent assassins to murder Yuan Ang, the former chancellor of Wu. Emperor Jing dispatched Tian Shu to investigate the affair in Liang. Tian Shu uncovered all the details and returned to deliver his report.
units.literal: King Xiao of Liang sent people to assassinate the former chancellor of Wu, Yuan Ang. Emperor Jing summoned Tian Shu to investigate Liang, and he obtained full details of the affair and returned to report.

units.zh: 景帝曰：「梁有之乎？」
units.en: Emperor Jing asked: "Is Liang truly responsible?"
units.literal: Emperor Jing said: "Did Liang do this?"

units.zh: 叔對曰：「死罪！
units.en: Tian Shu replied: "I deserve death for what I must say!
units.literal: Tian Shu replied: "A capital offense to say so!

units.zh: 有之。」
units.en: It is true."
units.literal: It is so."

units.zh: 上曰：「其事安在？」
units.en: The emperor asked: "Where is the evidence of the case?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Where is the evidence?"

units.zh: 田叔曰：「上毋以梁事為也。」
units.en: Tian Shu said: "Your Majesty must not pursue the matter of Liang any further."
units.literal: Tian Shu said: "Your Majesty should not pursue the Liang matter."

units.zh: 上曰：「何也？」
units.en: The emperor asked: "Why not?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Why?"

units.zh: 曰：「今梁王不伏誅，是漢法不行也；
units.en: He replied: "If the King of Liang is not brought to justice, it means the laws of the Han dynasty hold no authority.
units.literal: He said: "If the King of Liang is not put to death, then Han law is not being carried out;

units.zh: 如其伏法，而太后食不甘味，臥不安席，此憂在陛下也。」
units.en: But should he be made to face the law, the Empress Dowager will find no pleasure in her meals and no rest in her bed—and that burden will fall squarely upon Your Majesty."
units.literal: But if he submits to the law, then the Empress Dowager will find no flavor in her food and no comfort in her bed—this worry would rest upon Your Majesty."

units.zh: 景帝大賢之，以為魯相。
units.en: Emperor Jing was deeply impressed by his wisdom and appointed him as the Chancellor of Lu.
units.literal: Emperor Jing greatly esteemed him as worthy and appointed him as chancellor of Lu.

units.zh: 魯相初到，民自言相，訟王取其財物百餘人。
units.en: When Tian Shu first arrived in Lu as chancellor, more than a hundred of the common people came forward on their own to bring suit, accusing the king of seizing their property.
units.literal: When the chancellor of Lu first arrived, the people came to address the chancellor themselves, with more than a hundred suing the king for taking their property.

units.zh: 田叔取其渠率二十人，各笞五十，餘各搏二十，怒之曰：「王非若主邪？
units.en: Tian Shu seized twenty of the ringleaders and had each given fifty strokes of the bamboo rod. The rest he had struck twenty times apiece. He rebuked them furiously: "Is the king not your sovereign lord?
units.literal: Tian Shu took twenty of their ringleaders and gave each fifty lashes with a rod, and struck the rest each twenty times, scolding them angrily: "Is the king not your lord?

units.zh: 何自敢言若主！」
units.en: How dare you presume to bring accusations against your own lord!"
units.literal: How dare you presume to speak against your lord!"

units.zh: 魯王聞之大慚，發中府錢，使相償之。
units.en: When the King of Lu heard of this, he was deeply ashamed. He opened the inner treasury and ordered the chancellor to use the funds to compensate the people.
units.literal: When the King of Lu heard this, he was greatly ashamed, and released money from the inner treasury, ordering the chancellor to compensate them.

units.zh: 相曰：「王自奪之，使相償之，是王為惡而相為善也。
units.en: The chancellor said: "Your Majesty seized these goods yourself, yet now you order the chancellor to make restitution. This would make the king appear the villain and the chancellor the virtuous one.
units.literal: The chancellor said: "The king himself took their property, and now makes the chancellor compensate them—this makes the king appear evil while the chancellor appears good.

units.zh: 相毋與償之。」
units.en: The chancellor will have no part in repaying them."
units.literal: The chancellor should not participate in compensating them."

units.zh: 於是王乃盡償之。
units.en: And so the king himself repaid every one of them in full.
units.literal: Thereupon the king himself repaid them all in full.

units.zh: 魯王好獵，相常從入苑中，王輒休相就館舍，相出，常暴坐待王苑外。
units.en: The King of Lu was fond of hunting. The chancellor would regularly accompany him into the royal hunting park, but each time the king would dismiss him to rest at the guest quarters. Instead, the chancellor would go outside and sit exposed to the elements, waiting for the king beyond the park walls.
units.literal: The King of Lu loved hunting. The chancellor would often follow him into the hunting park. The king would always dismiss the chancellor to rest at the lodgings, but the chancellor would go out and sit exposed in the open, waiting for the king outside the park.

units.zh: 王數使人請相休，終不休，曰：「我王暴露苑中，我獨何為就舍！」
units.en: The king sent messengers several times urging the chancellor to go inside and rest, but Tian Shu refused every time, saying: "While my king endures the elements out in the park, why should I alone seek the comfort of a roof!"
units.literal: The king sent people several times to ask the chancellor to rest, but he refused to the end, saying: "My king is out in the open in the park—why should I alone go to rest at the lodgings!"

units.zh: 魯王以故不大出游。
units.en: Because of this, the King of Lu greatly curtailed his hunting excursions.
units.literal: For this reason, the King of Lu no longer went on great hunting excursions.

units.zh: 數年，叔以官卒，魯以百金祠，少子仁不受也，曰：「不以百金傷先人名。」
units.en: After several years, Tian Shu died while still in office. The state of Lu offered a hundred pieces of gold for a memorial shrine in his honor, but his youngest son Tian Ren refused the gift, saying: "I will not let a hundred pieces of gold tarnish my father's good name."
units.literal: After several years, Shu died in office. Lu offered a hundred gold pieces for his memorial shrine, but his youngest son Ren refused to accept them, saying: "I will not let a hundred gold pieces tarnish my father's name."

units.zh: 仁以壯健為衛將軍舍人，數從擊匈奴。
units.en: Tian Ren, strong and robust in build, served as a retainer in the household of the General of the Guard, and accompanied him on repeated campaigns against the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Ren, being strong and vigorous, served as a retainer of the General of the Guard, and accompanied him several times to attack the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 衛將軍進言仁，仁為郎中。
units.en: The General of the Guard put forward a recommendation for Tian Ren, who was then appointed as a Gentleman of the Palace.
units.literal: The General of the Guard recommended Ren, and Ren was made a court gentleman.

units.zh: 數歲，為二千石丞相長史，失官。
units.en: After some years, he rose to the position of Senior Secretary to the Chancellor, a rank worth two thousand bushels, but subsequently lost the post.
units.literal: After several years, he served as a two-thousand-bushel-ranked Senior Secretary to the Chancellor, but lost his position.

units.zh: 其後使刺舉三河。
units.en: Later, he was dispatched to inspect and impeach corrupt officials in the Three Rivers region.
units.literal: Afterwards he was sent to investigate and impeach officials in the Three Rivers region.

units.zh: 上東巡，仁奏事有辭，上說，拜為京輔都尉。
units.en: When the emperor went on his eastern inspection tour, Tian Ren presented his reports with such eloquence that the emperor was delighted and appointed him as the Commandant of the Capital Suburbs.
units.literal: When the emperor went on an eastern tour, Ren reported on affairs with eloquence; the emperor was pleased and appointed him as Commandant of the Capital Suburbs.

units.zh: 月餘，上遷拜為司直。
units.en: A little over a month later, the emperor promoted him again to the office of Director of Justice.
units.literal: After more than a month, the emperor further promoted him and appointed him as Director of Justice.

units.zh: 數歲，坐太子事。
units.en: Some years later, he became entangled in the affair of the Crown Prince.
units.literal: After several years, he was implicated in the affair of the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 時左相自將兵，令司直田仁主閉守城門，坐縱太子，下吏誅死。
units.en: At the time, the Left Chancellor personally took command of the troops and ordered the Director of Justice, Tian Ren, to close and guard the city gates. Tian Ren was convicted of allowing the Crown Prince to escape, handed over to the judicial officials, and put to death.
units.literal: At that time the Left Chancellor personally led troops and ordered the Director of Justice Tian Ren to take charge of closing and guarding the city gates. Tian Ren was convicted of letting the Crown Prince escape, handed over to officials, and executed.

units.zh: 仁發兵，長陵令車千秋上變仁，仁族死。
units.en: Tian Ren had also taken up arms in the affair; the Magistrate of Changling, Che Qianqiu, submitted a memorial denouncing him for treason, and Tian Ren's entire clan was put to death.
units.literal: Tian Ren had also mobilized troops in the affair; the magistrate of Changling, Che Qianqiu, submitted a memorial reporting his treason, and Tian Ren's entire clan was executed.

units.zh: 陘城今在中山國。
units.en: The town of Xingcheng is now situated within the kingdom of Zhongshan.
units.literal: Xingcheng is now in the kingdom of Zhongshan.

units.zh: 太史公曰：孔子稱曰「居是國必聞其政」，田叔之謂乎！
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Confucius once said, "One who dwells in a state will surely learn of its governance"—was he not speaking of a man like Tian Shu!
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Confucius said, "Living in a state, one must be informed of its governance"—was this not said of someone like Tian Shu!

units.zh: 義不忘賢，明主之美以救過。
units.en: He upheld righteousness by never neglecting men of worth, and he extolled the virtues of his enlightened sovereign while working to remedy the ruler's faults.
units.literal: By righteousness he did not forget the worthy, and praised the virtues of an enlightened sovereign so as to remedy faults.

units.zh: 仁與余善，余故并論之。
units.en: Tian Ren and I were on friendly terms, and so I have included his account here alongside his father's.
units.literal: Ren was on good terms with me, so I have discussed them together.

units.zh: 褚先生曰：臣為郎時，聞之曰田仁故與任安相善。
units.en: Master Chu says: When I served as a Gentleman of the Palace, I heard that Tian Ren had once been close friends with Ren An.
units.literal: Master Chu says: When I served as a court gentleman, I heard it said that Tian Ren had originally been on good terms with Ren An.

units.zh: 任安，滎陽人也。
units.en: Ren An was a native of Xingyang.
units.literal: Ren An was a person from Xingyang.

units.zh: 少孤貧困，為人將車之長安，留，求事為小吏，未有因緣也，因占著名數。
units.en: Orphaned young and mired in poverty, he drove a cart for a traveler heading to Chang'an and remained there, seeking a position as a minor official. Having no connections to rely upon, he registered his name on the rolls of a local district.
units.literal: Orphaned young and in poverty, he drove a cart for someone to Chang'an, stayed there, and sought service as a minor official, but had no connections; he then registered his name on the rolls of a local district.

units.zh: 武功，扶風西界小邑也，谷口蜀道近山。
units.en: Wugong was a small town on the western frontier of the Fufeng commandery, nestled near the mountains where the valley road led toward Shu.
units.literal: Wugong was a small town on the western border of Fufeng, near the mountains at the mouth of the valley on the road to Shu.

units.zh: 安以為武功小邑，無豪，易高也，安留，代人為求盜亭父。
units.en: Ren An reckoned that since Wugong was a small town with no powerful local families, it would be an easy place to distinguish himself. He settled there and took up a post as a thief-catcher at the local station, replacing the previous man.
units.literal: An considered that Wugong, being a small town with no powerful families, would be a place where he could easily rise to prominence. So An stayed there and took a position replacing someone as a thief-catcher at the local station.

units.zh: 後為亭長。
units.en: In time, he rose to become the station chief.
units.literal: Later he became station chief.

units.zh: 邑中人民俱出獵，任安常為人分麋鹿雉兔，部署老小當壯劇易處，眾人皆喜，曰：「無傷也，任少卿分別平，有智略。」
units.en: Whenever the people of the town went out together to hunt, Ren An would take charge of distributing the game—elk, deer, pheasants, and rabbits—among the hunters. He would assign the elderly and the young to the easier stations and the able-bodied men to the more difficult ones. Everyone was delighted and said: "All is well—Ren Shaoqing apportions things fairly and shows real shrewdness and judgment."
units.literal: When the townspeople all went out to hunt, Ren An would always divide the elk, deer, pheasants, and rabbits among them, and assign the old and young and the strong to the difficult and easy positions. Everyone was pleased and said: "No harm done—Ren Shaoqing divides things fairly and has wisdom and good judgment."

units.zh: 明日復合會，會者數百人。
units.en: The following day, the people gathered once more, several hundred strong.
units.literal: The next day they assembled again, with several hundred people at the gathering.

units.zh: 任少卿曰：「某子甲何為不來乎？」
units.en: Ren Shaoqing asked: "Why has such-and-such a person not come?"
units.literal: Ren Shaoqing said: "Why has so-and-so not come?"

units.zh: 諸人皆怪其見之疾也。
units.en: Everyone marveled at how swiftly he had spotted the missing person.
units.literal: Everyone marveled at how quickly he had noticed the absence.

units.zh: 其後除為三老，舉為親民，出為三百石長，治民。
units.en: After this, he was appointed as a Village Elder, recommended for his closeness to the common people, and eventually sent out to serve as a magistrate at the three-hundred-bushel rank, governing the local populace.
units.literal: Afterwards he was appointed as an Elder, recommended as one close to the people, and went out to serve as a three-hundred-bushel magistrate, governing the people.

units.zh: 坐上行出游共帳不辦，斥免。
units.en: He was convicted of failing to properly prepare the communal tent when the emperor passed through the area on a tour, and was dismissed from office.
units.literal: He was convicted of failing to properly arrange the shared canopy when the emperor passed through on a tour, and was dismissed.

units.zh: 乃為衛將軍舍人，與田仁會，俱為舍人，居門下，同心相愛。
units.en: He then entered service as a retainer in the household of the General of the Guard, where he met Tian Ren. Both served as retainers under the same roof, and they became fast friends, united in heart.
units.literal: He then became a retainer of the General of the Guard, where he met Tian Ren. Both served as retainers, living under the same roof, and were of one mind in their affection for each other.

units.zh: 此二人家貧，無錢用以事將軍家監，家監使養惡齧馬。
units.en: Both men came from poor families and had no money to offer the general's household steward, so the steward assigned them to tend the most ill-tempered and vicious horses.
units.literal: Both men's families were poor, and they had no money to bribe the general's household steward, so the steward assigned them to tend the vicious, biting horses.

units.zh: 兩人同床臥，仁竊言曰：「不知人哉家監也！」
units.en: The two men shared a bed at night. Tian Ren whispered bitterly: "What a poor judge of men the household steward is!"
units.literal: The two men shared a bed, and Ren whispered: "The household steward has no eye for talent!"

units.zh: 任安曰：「將軍尚不知人，何乃家監也！」
units.en: Ren An replied: "Even the general himself has no eye for talent—why blame the household steward!"
units.literal: Ren An said: "Even the general himself does not know men—let alone the household steward!"

units.zh: 衛將軍從此兩人過平陽主，主家令兩人與騎奴同席而食，此二子拔刀列斷席別坐。
units.en: When the General of the Guard took these two men along on a visit to Princess Pingyang, the princess's household staff ordered them to share a dining mat with the mounted slaves. The two men drew their swords, slashed the mat in two, and took their seats apart from the slaves.
units.literal: The General of the Guard brought these two men along when he visited Princess Pingyang. The princess's household ordered the two to sit and eat at the same mat with the mounted slaves, but the two men drew their swords, cut the mat in two, and sat apart.

units.zh: 主家皆怪而惡之，莫敢呵。
units.en: Everyone in the princess's household was shocked and disapproving, but none dared to rebuke them.
units.literal: The princess's entire household was astonished and offended, but none dared to reprimand them.

units.zh: 其後有詔募擇衛將軍舍人以為郎，將軍取舍人中富給者，令具鞌馬絳衣玉具劍，欲入奏之。
units.en: Later, an imperial edict was issued to recruit and select retainers of the General of the Guard for appointment as Gentlemen at court. The general chose the wealthiest among his retainers and ordered them to furnish themselves with saddled horses, crimson robes, and jade-hilted swords, intending to present them before the emperor.
units.literal: Afterwards there was an imperial edict to recruit and select retainers of the General of the Guard to serve as gentlemen at court. The general chose the wealthy and well-provisioned among his retainers, ordering them to prepare saddled horses, crimson robes, and jade-handled swords, intending to present them to the emperor.

units.zh: 會賢大夫少府趙禹來過衛將軍，將軍呼所舉舍人以示趙禹。
units.en: It happened that the esteemed official Zhao Yu, who served as Privy Treasurer, paid a visit to the General of the Guard. The general summoned the retainers he had selected and presented them for Zhao Yu's inspection.
units.literal: It happened that the worthy senior official Zhao Yu, the Privy Treasurer, came to visit the General of the Guard. The general called forth the retainers he had selected to show them to Zhao Yu.

units.zh: 趙禹以次問之，十餘人無一人習事有智略者。
units.en: Zhao Yu questioned them one by one, and among the ten or more candidates, not a single one showed any experience in administration or possessed any measure of wit and strategic ability.
units.literal: Zhao Yu questioned them one by one, and among the ten or more men, not a single one was experienced in affairs or possessed wisdom and strategic ability.

units.zh: 趙禹曰：「吾聞之，將門之下必有將類。
units.en: Zhao Yu said: "I have always heard it said that under the roof of a great general, one is sure to find men of a general's caliber.
units.literal: Zhao Yu said: "I have heard that beneath the gates of a general, there must be men of a general's caliber.

units.zh: 傳曰『不知其君視其所使，不知其子視其所友』。
units.en: As the saying goes, 'To know a lord, observe whom he employs; to know a son, observe whom he befriends.'
units.literal: The tradition says, 'If you do not know a lord, look at whom he employs; if you do not know a son, look at who his friends are.'

units.zh: 今有詔舉將軍舍人者，欲以觀將軍而能得賢者文武之士也。
units.en: The purpose of this edict to select retainers from the general's household is to evaluate the general himself—to see whether he has the ability to identify worthy men of both civil and military talent.
units.literal: Now there is an edict to select retainers of the general, the purpose being to observe the general and see whether he can identify worthy men of both civil and military ability.

units.zh: 今徒取盎人子上之，又無智略，如木偶人衣之綺繡耳，將柰之何？」
units.en: Yet you have merely picked the sons of the wealthy to put forward, and they lack any wit or strategic ability—they are nothing more than wooden puppets dressed in fine silk. What purpose will they serve?"
units.literal: Now you have merely taken the sons of wealthy men and put them forward, yet they lack wisdom and strategy—they are like wooden puppets dressed in fine silks. What good will this do?"

units.zh: 於是趙禹悉召衛將軍舍人百餘人，以次問之，得田仁、任安，曰：「獨此兩人可耳，餘無可用者。」
units.en: Zhao Yu then summoned all the general's retainers—over a hundred—and questioned them one after another. He singled out Tian Ren and Ren An, declaring: "Only these two are fit for service. The rest are of no use whatsoever."
units.literal: Thereupon Zhao Yu summoned all of the General of the Guard's retainers, over a hundred of them, and questioned them one by one. He identified Tian Ren and Ren An, saying: "Only these two will do; the rest are of no use."

units.zh: 衛將軍見此兩人貧，意不平。
units.en: The General of the Guard, seeing how poor the two men were, was not at all pleased.
units.literal: When the General of the Guard saw that these two men were poor, he was displeased.

units.zh: 趙禹去，謂兩人曰：「各自具樾象絳衣。」
units.en: After Zhao Yu departed, the general told the two men: "Each of you must furnish your own saddled horses and crimson robes yourselves."
units.literal: After Zhao Yu left, the general told the two men: "Each of you must prepare your own saddled horses and crimson robes at your own expense."

units.zh: 兩人對曰：「家貧無用具也。」
units.en: The two men replied: "Our families are too poor. We have no means to provide such equipment."
units.literal: The two men replied: "Our families are poor, and we have no means to furnish such things."

units.zh: 將軍怒曰：「今兩君家自為貧，何為出此言？
units.en: The general said angrily: "So your families are poor—why then do you speak like this?
units.literal: The general said angrily: "If your families are truly poor, why do you speak such words?

units.zh: 鞅鞅如有移德於我者，何也？」
units.en: You carry yourselves with such resentment, as though I owed you some debt of gratitude you had earned—why is that?"
units.literal: You act resentful, as though you had bestowed some favor on me that I have failed to repay—why is that?"

units.zh: 將軍不得已，上籍以聞。
units.en: With no other option, the general submitted their names to the throne for consideration.
units.literal: The general had no choice but to submit their names on the register for the emperor to hear of.

units.zh: 有詔召見衛將軍舍人，此二人前見，詔問能略相推第也。
units.en: An imperial edict summoned the General of the Guard's retainers for an audience. The two men stepped forward, and the emperor commanded them to assess and rank each other's abilities.
units.literal: An edict was issued to summon the General of the Guard's retainers for an audience. These two came forward, and by imperial command were asked to evaluate and rank each other's abilities.

units.zh: 田仁對曰；
units.en: Tian Ren answered:
units.literal: Tian Ren replied:

units.zh: 「提桴鼓立軍門，使士大夫樂死戰鬬，仁不及任安。」
units.en: "When it comes to taking up the drumstick at the camp gate and inspiring officers and soldiers to fight gladly to the death—in this, I am no match for Ren An."
units.literal: "In taking up the drumstick to beat the war drum, standing at the gate of the camp, and inspiring officers and soldiers to gladly fight to the death—I, Ren, am no match for Ren An."

units.zh: 任安對曰：「夫決嫌疑，定是非，辯治官，使百姓無怨心，安不及仁也。」
units.en: Ren An replied: "When it comes to resolving doubts, determining right from wrong, evaluating the competence of officials, and ensuring that the common people harbor no resentment—in these things, I am no match for Tian Ren."
units.literal: Ren An replied: "In resolving doubts and suspicions, determining right and wrong, discerning the governance of officials, and ensuring the people harbor no resentment—I, An, am no match for Tian Ren."

units.zh: 武帝大笑曰：「善。」
units.en: Emperor Wu laughed heartily and said: "Well spoken."
units.literal: Emperor Wu laughed greatly and said: "Excellent."

units.zh: 使任安護北軍，使田仁護邊田穀於河上。
units.en: He assigned Ren An to oversee the Northern Army, and dispatched Tian Ren to supervise the frontier agricultural colonies along the Yellow River.
units.literal: He sent Ren An to oversee the Northern Army, and sent Tian Ren to oversee the border agricultural colonies along the Yellow River.

units.zh: 此兩人立名天下。
units.en: Through these appointments, both men made their names known throughout the empire.
units.literal: These two men established their reputations throughout the empire.

units.zh: 其後用任安為益州刺史，以田仁為丞相長史。
units.en: Subsequently, Ren An was appointed as the Regional Inspector of Yizhou, and Tian Ren was made the Senior Secretary to the Chancellor.
units.literal: Afterwards Ren An was appointed as Regional Inspector of Yizhou, and Tian Ren was made Senior Secretary to the Chancellor.

units.zh: 田仁上書言：「天下郡太守多為姦利，三河尤甚，臣請先刺舉三河。
units.en: Tian Ren submitted a memorial to the throne: "Many commandery governors throughout the empire engage in corruption for personal gain, and the Three Rivers region is the worst offender. I request permission to begin by investigating and impeaching the officials of the Three Rivers.
units.literal: Tian Ren submitted a memorial saying: "Many commandery governors throughout the empire engage in corrupt profiteering, and the Three Rivers region is the worst. I request permission to investigate and impeach the Three Rivers first.

units.zh: 三河太守皆內倚中貴人，與三公有親屬，無所畏憚，宜先正三河以警天下姦吏。」
units.en: The governors of the Three Rivers all rely on the backing of powerful palace favorites and are related by kinship to the Three Excellencies. They know no fear. We should first set the Three Rivers right as a warning to corrupt officials across the empire."
units.literal: The governors of the Three Rivers all rely internally on powerful court favorites and are related to the Three Excellencies; they fear nothing. We should first rectify the Three Rivers to serve as a warning to corrupt officials throughout the empire."

units.zh: 是時河南、河內太守皆御史大夫杜父兄子弟也，河東太守石丞相子孫也。
units.en: At that time, the governors of Henan and Henei were all kinsmen—fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews—of Grand Censor Du, and the Governor of Hedong was a descendant of the former Chancellor Shi.
units.literal: At that time, the governors of Henan and Henei were all fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews of Grand Censor Du, and the governor of Hedong was a descendant of Chancellor Shi.

units.zh: 是時石氏九人為二千石，方盛貴。
units.en: At that time, nine members of the Shi clan held offices at the two-thousand-bushel rank, and the family was at the very peak of its power and prestige.
units.literal: At that time, nine members of the Shi clan held positions at the two-thousand-bushel rank, and the family was at the height of its power and prestige.

units.zh: 田仁數上書言之。
units.en: Tian Ren submitted memorial after memorial pressing the case.
units.literal: Tian Ren repeatedly submitted memorials speaking of this matter.

units.zh: 杜大夫及石氏使人謝，謂田少卿曰：「吾非敢有語言也，願少卿無相誣汙也。」
units.en: Grand Censor Du and the Shi clan sent intermediaries to plead with him, telling Tian Ren: "We would not dare utter a word against you. We only hope that you will not level false accusations against us."
units.literal: Grand Censor Du and the Shi clan sent people to make apologies, telling Tian Shaoqing: "We would not dare say anything against you; we only hope that you, Shaoqing, will not falsely accuse and defame us."

units.zh: 仁已刺三河，三河太守皆下吏誅死。
units.en: Tian Ren carried out his investigation of the Three Rivers, and all three governors were handed over to the judicial officials and put to death.
units.literal: Ren investigated the Three Rivers, and all three governors were handed over to officials and executed.

units.zh: 仁還奏事，武帝說，以仁為能不畏彊御，拜仁為丞相司直，威振天下。
units.en: Tian Ren returned and delivered his report. Emperor Wu was delighted, judging Tian Ren to be a man who feared no authority however powerful. He appointed him as the Chancellor's Director of Justice, and his renown shook the entire empire.
units.literal: Ren returned and reported on the matter. Emperor Wu was pleased, considered Ren capable and unafraid of the powerful, and appointed him as the Chancellor's Director of Justice; his authority shook the empire.

units.zh: 其後逢太子有兵事，丞相自將兵，使司直主城門。
units.en: Later, the crisis came when the Crown Prince took up arms. The Chancellor personally led troops and ordered the Director of Justice to take charge of guarding the city gates.
units.literal: Afterwards it happened that the Crown Prince was involved in a military affair. The Chancellor personally led troops and ordered the Director of Justice to take charge of the city gates.

units.zh: 司直以為太子骨肉之親，父子之閒不甚欲近，去之諸陵過。
units.en: The Director of Justice felt that since the Crown Prince was the emperor's own flesh and blood, this was a dispute between father and son that he had no wish to be drawn into. He left his post and detoured past the imperial tombs.
units.literal: The Director of Justice considered that since the Crown Prince was of the emperor's own flesh and blood, and the matter between father and son was not something he greatly wished to involve himself in, he departed and passed by the imperial tombs.

units.zh: 是時武帝在甘泉，使御史大夫暴君下責丞相「何為縱太子」，丞相對言「使司直部守城門而開太子」。
units.en: At the time, Emperor Wu was at the Ganquan Palace. He dispatched Grand Censor Bao Shengzhi to reprimand the Chancellor: "Why did you allow the Crown Prince to escape?" The Chancellor replied in his defense: "I assigned the Director of Justice to guard the city gates, but he opened them and let the Crown Prince through."
units.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was at Ganquan. He sent Grand Censor Bao Shengzhi down to reprimand the Chancellor: "Why did you let the Crown Prince escape?" The Chancellor replied: "I ordered the Director of Justice to guard the city gates, but he opened them for the Crown Prince."

units.zh: 上書以聞，請捕系司直。
units.en: A memorial was submitted to the emperor requesting the arrest and imprisonment of the Director of Justice.
units.literal: A memorial was submitted to bring the matter to the emperor's attention, requesting the arrest and imprisonment of the Director of Justice.

units.zh: 司直下吏，誅死。
units.en: The Director of Justice was handed over to the judicial officials and put to death.
units.literal: The Director of Justice was handed over to officials and executed.

units.zh: 是時任安為北軍使者護軍，太子立車北軍南門外，召任安，與節令發兵。
units.en: At that time, Ren An was serving as the Protector General dispatched to the Northern Army. The Crown Prince halted his carriage outside the south gate of the Northern Army camp, summoned Ren An, and presented him with an imperial tally ordering him to mobilize the troops.
units.literal: At that time Ren An was serving as the Protector General dispatched to the Northern Army. The Crown Prince stopped his carriage outside the south gate of the Northern Army camp, summoned Ren An, and gave him a tally commanding him to mobilize troops.

units.zh: 安拜受節，入，閉門不出。
units.en: Ren An bowed and accepted the tally, then entered the camp, shut the gates behind him, and did not come out.
units.literal: An bowed and accepted the tally, entered the camp, closed the gates, and did not come out.

units.zh: 武帝聞之，以為任安為詳邪，不傅事，何也？
units.en: When Emperor Wu heard of this, he suspected Ren An of feigning loyalty: the man had accepted the tally yet taken no action and reported nothing to the throne—why?
units.literal: When Emperor Wu heard of this, he thought Ren An had been feigning righteousness and had not reported the matter—why?

units.zh: 任安笞辱北軍錢官小吏，小吏上書言之，以為受太子節，言「幸與我其鮮好者」。
units.en: Ren An had previously flogged and humiliated a minor financial clerk of the Northern Army. The aggrieved clerk submitted a memorial denouncing him, testifying that Ren An had accepted the Crown Prince's tally and had demanded to be given "the freshest and finest goods."
units.literal: Ren An had flogged and humiliated a minor financial official of the Northern Army. The minor official submitted a memorial reporting this, saying that An had accepted the Crown Prince's tally and had said, "Please give me the freshest and finest goods."

units.zh: 書上聞，武帝曰：「是老吏也，見兵事起，欲坐觀成敗，見勝者欲合從之，有兩心。
units.en: When the memorial came to the emperor's attention, Emperor Wu declared: "He is a wily old official. When the fighting broke out, he wanted to sit back and watch how things unfolded, intending to side with whichever faction won. He harbors a divided heart.
units.literal: When the memorial reached the emperor's ears, Emperor Wu said: "This is an old and cunning official. When the military conflict arose, he wanted to sit and watch the outcome, intending to join whichever side prevailed. He harbors divided loyalties.

units.zh: 安有當死之罪甚眾，吾常活之，今懷詐，有不忠之心。」
units.en: Ren An has committed many offenses deserving death, yet I have always spared his life. Now he harbors treachery in his breast and is disloyal at heart."
units.literal: An has accumulated many crimes deserving of death, yet I have always spared his life. Now he harbors deceit and has a disloyal heart."

units.zh: 下安吏，誅死。
units.en: Ren An was handed over to the judicial officials and put to death.
units.literal: An was handed over to officials and executed.

units.zh: 夫月滿則虧，物盛則衰，天地之常也。
units.en: When the moon reaches fullness, it begins to wane; when things reach their zenith, they begin to decline. Such is the immutable law of heaven and earth.
units.literal: When the moon is full it wanes; when things reach their peak they decline—this is the constant way of heaven and earth.

units.zh: 知進而不知退，久乘富貴，禍積為祟。
units.en: Those who know only how to advance and never how to retreat, who cling to wealth and honor too long, find that their misfortunes pile up until disaster strikes.
units.literal: Knowing how to advance but not how to retreat, riding wealth and honor for too long—calamity accumulates and becomes a curse.

units.zh: 故范蠡之去越，辭不受官位，名傳後世，萬歲不忘，豈可及哉！
units.en: Thus, did Fan Li, when he departed from Yue and refused all titles and offices, leave a name that would be passed down through the ages, unforgotten for ten thousand years. Who could ever rival such a man!
units.literal: Thus, Fan Li's departure from Yue—declining office and refusing rank—caused his name to be transmitted to later generations, never forgotten for ten thousand years. How can anyone match him!

units.zh: 後進者慎戒之。
units.en: Let those who come after take heed and learn from this lesson.
units.literal: Those who come after should take careful warning from this.
